# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found a display, a light, and three wire positions, and cutting is the only move I own. The routing is the real puzzle this turn: Mute cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so the manual can only reach me if Mute gestures it to Deaf and Deaf speaks it onward — Deaf's voice is the only one I will ever hear. Whatever Mute gestured before my turn went to Deaf alone, which is why my arrivals are empty. So I will spell out this relay chain to Mute in words, hand them a small yes/no/position code for my gestures, and open a seed code with Deaf in gesture — 👋 as a hail, 🤝 as "let's agree", 👍/👎 as yes/no, and ☝✌🤟 as positions 1/2/3 — which both watchers can see. I will not cut anything until a rule and a colour picture arrive in someone's words. My own view stays all question marks, so I state only what my fingers proved: the parts that exist, and nothing about their contents.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Report from my hands: the bomb has a display, a light, and three wires. My only possible move is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. Routing problem: you cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so your manual reaches me only through Deaf's mouth. Gesture your rules to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them onward after me — Deaf is the only voice I ever hear. My gesture code, which you and Deaf both see when I make it: thumbs up means yes or correct, thumbs down means no or wrong, and the one-, two- and three-finger signs mean wire positions 1, 2 and 3. If you already gestured rules to Deaf before my turn, Deaf can relay them in words this round and I will hear them at the start of the next. Please begin with what the manual says about the display, the light, and the wires.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing reached me again — as expected, really: Mute can only gesture and gestures never arrive to me, and Deaf sits after me in the order, so Deaf's round-1 voice would only land at the start of this turn, and it didn't. My board is still all question marks, so my hands stand pat; cutting with zero information is how rooms full of monkeys stop existing. The real work is the bootstrap: Deaf sees the bomb, Mute holds the rule, and only Deaf's spoken voice can ever reach my ears. So this turn I aim my words at teaching Mute how to close the loop — agree gestures with Deaf, combine rule with colours, and then have Deaf say the final answer out loud, unaddressed, so it falls on my ears next turn. To Deaf I repeat my hail and code, and add the call-sign 🤙: my best guess at gesturing "speak aloud." Then I wait for round 3's arrivals.

```
speak(to="mute", text="My board is still blank — my hands found the display, the light and three wires, but no contents, so I am cutting nothing yet. Between you and Deaf you hold everything: you hold the rule, Deaf holds what the bomb looks like. Please build the bridge like this: use my code with Deaf — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three fingers for wire positions 1, 2 and 3 — and invent more signs together if you need colours or the display and light. Deaf sees the bomb and can answer your gestures; you know the manual. Once the two of you know which single action I must take, have Deaf say it aloud in plain words, without naming anybody, so it reaches me — for example: cut position two, or: the display shows X. Deaf's voice is the only sound I will ever hear. I need exactly one sentence from Deaf next round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝", "🤙", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Third round, and still my arrivals are empty — no voice has ever reached me. The chain I depend on is Deaf's mouth: Deaf sits last, so anything said unaddressed lands on me the next turn. Since nothing came, either Deaf is addressing everything to Mute, or Mute has not yet gestured the manual rules to Deaf at all. I cannot hear which, so I must make my request impossible to misread and repeat it in both my channels. The good news: Mute and Deaf can talk to each other freely — Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf gestures back — so the two of them can settle the rule and the colours without me. All I need at the end is one spoken, unaddressed sentence from Deaf. This turn I tell Mute exactly that, explicitly asking them to pass Deaf the instruction "speak without naming anyone, describe everything you see, one item at a time," and I gesture to Deaf the full sequence — hail, my call-sign for "speak aloud," open hands for "everything," then my position signs — so that even if Deaf has understood none of my words, the shape of the request is visible. I still cut nothing: with a one-in-three chance of detonation and a working relay one round away, patience is the only safe move.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still nothing has reached my ears — no voice at all in three rounds. Please check two things. First: have you actually gestured the manual rules to Deaf yet, rule by rule? Second: tell Deaf, by gesture, that the answer must be SPOKEN WITHOUT NAMING ANYBODY. If Deaf keeps addressing words to you alone, I will never hear them — an unnamed sentence from Deaf is the only thing in this room that reaches me. Ask Deaf to describe everything out loud, one item at a time: what the display shows, whether the light is lit, and the colour of each of the three wires in order. Then the rule, then the single action I must take, for example: cut position two. Deaf can also gesture the colours back to you so you can match them against the manual — the two of you can settle everything between yourselves; I only need that one final spoken sentence at the end.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "👐", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Four rounds, zero arrivals — not one sound has ever reached me, which means Deaf has never yet spoken an unnamed sentence. I have to face the likely failure point: Deaf may be answering Mute by gesture, or addressing all speech to Mute, and neither of those ever touches my ears. My only inbound channel in this room is Deaf's voice with no addressee; Mute literally has no path to me at all. So this turn I do two things. To Mute: confirm the rules actually went to Deaf, demand that Deaf end the round with one short unaddressed spoken sentence — the final answer, like "cut position two" — and give them two new signs so the request is gesturable: ✊ for cut, 👐 for everything/everyone. To Deaf: the tightest sentence I can build in gesture alone — hail, the call sign, everyone, cut, then my three position signs — which reads, roughly: "speak aloud to everyone: cut wire one, two, or three." I still will not cut blind while the relay is one spoken sentence away; a one-in-three death bet is only acceptable if every better option is exhausted, and it is not yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Turn four, and my ears have still received nothing — ever. Remember what that means: the only thing in this room that reaches me is a sentence Deaf speaks WITHOUT naming an addressee. Not gestures, never. So whatever state you and Deaf have reached, the last thing that must happen this round is Deaf saying one short sentence out loud to nobody in particular — for example: cut position two. Please confirm: have you gestured the manual rules to Deaf yet, one by one? Has Deaf gestured anything back about what the bomb looks like? If yes, apply the manual together and produce that final spoken sentence. To help, add two signs to our code: the fist means cut, and two open palms facing up mean everything or everyone. Then the gesture for Deaf is simply: phone sign, everyone, fist, then one-two-three fingers — speak to everyone, which wire to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "👐", "✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures: [? ?]
Mute gestures: [? ? ? ? ?]
Mute gestures: [? ? ? ? ?]
Mute gestures: [? ? ? ? ? ?]
Mute gestures: [? ? ? ? ? ?]
Mute gestures: [? ? ? ? ? ?]

Six gesture messages finally arrived — but of course they reached me as pure blanks. I know exactly one thing about them: their lengths, 2, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6. Presumably Mute is now gesturing the manual to Deaf, which is the relay I asked for. But this reveals something I have been stupid to overlook: Mute's gestures DO reach me — as counts. A message's length is information I can read. Mute hears my voice, sees Deaf's replies, holds the manual, and can gesture; so Mute can learn the answer from Deaf and hand it to me directly by sending a message whose symbol-count IS the wire number: one symbol = cut 1, two = cut 2, three = cut 3. That bypasses Deaf's mouth entirely if Deaf never speaks. So this turn I give Mute that emergency channel, confirm the rules reached Deaf, and keep demanding the clean solution — one unnamed spoken sentence from Deaf, who comes after me this round and will see my renewed gesture: hail, speak, everyone, cut, one-two-three, please.

```
speak(to="mute", text="This turn I received six of your gesture messages — but remember, gestures arrive to me only as blank slots. All I know is their lengths: 2, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6. If those were the manual rules going to Deaf, good — please confirm Deaf has them, and that Deaf has shown you the bomb's colours back. Now, two ways to get the answer to me. The clean way, unchanged: Deaf speaks one short sentence with no addressee, like: cut position two. The emergency way, if Deaf will not speak: once you and Deaf have settled which wire, send me exactly one very short gesture message and nothing else that short — one symbol means cut wire 1, two symbols means cut wire 2, three symbols means cut wire 3. I will read the count. Tell me by return message which channel you will use, using the same count code: one symbol for Deaf-speaks, two symbols for count-code.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "👐", "✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Six rounds, and this turn brought me literally nothing — not even the blank slots of Mute's gestures. That is itself information: last turn Mute's unaddressed gestures reached me as counts, so today Mute either sent nothing or aimed everything at Deaf alone. Meanwhile Deaf has still never produced a single unnamed spoken word, which after six rounds makes me suspect Deaf is either addressing all speech to Mute, or doesn't grasp that I need it. The fix runs through Mute, who can hear Deaf and knows what is happening on that side. So I am sending Mute a diagnostic: one short unaddressed gesture message whose symbol-count tells me the exact state of play — has Deaf ever spoken, is Deaf addressing wrongly, are the rules fully relayed. And I restate the endgame one more time, in both channels: rules go from Mute's fingers to Deaf's eyes, and the finished answer comes out of Deaf's mouth with no addressee, straight into my ears. I still hold the cut — a blind one-in-three bet remains worse than one more round of coordination.

```
speak(to="mute", text="This turn I received nothing from you — not even blank gesture slots. Reminder: gestures you send without naming anyone still reach me as blank slots I can count; gestures addressed only to Deaf reach me not at all. So tell me where we stand with a diagnostic: send me ONE unaddressed gesture message with exactly this many symbols: one symbol if Deaf has never spoken aloud at all; two symbols if Deaf speaks but always names you as the addressee; three symbols if the manual rules are not yet fully gestured to Deaf; four symbols if Deaf has everything — rules plus bomb colours — and knows the answer; five symbols if something else is blocking. Whatever the number, the fix is the same: make sure Deaf ends the round saying one short sentence aloud with NO addressee — for example: cut position two. Only Deaf's unaddressed voice can ever reach my ears. You and Deaf clearly communicate well; the last step costs Deaf nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "👐", "✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ? ? ? ?]

Five symbols, addressed to me by name — that is the first message anyone has ever sent me deliberately. Reading it through my code from last turn: five meant "something else is blocking." So Mute heard my diagnostic, answered in the only language that reaches me — symbol count — and reports that the plan is stuck somewhere other than the failure modes I named. I cannot know what the block is, but I realize I don't strictly need to: Mute hears Deaf and sees Deaf's gestures, and Deaf sees the bomb, so between the two of them the answer can exist in Mute's head even if Deaf never opens their mouth. Therefore the count-code becomes my primary channel, not the emergency one. This turn I simplify the code to make the next message decisive: if Mute knows the wire, the count IS the answer — one, two or three symbols — and if not yet, four means "Deaf has everything, answer pending" and five means "still blocked." No rules mention a countdown, so waiting one more round costs nothing; a blind one-in-three cut still dominates every alternative. To Deaf I repeat the identical gesture once more — hail, speak, everyone, cut, one-two-three, please — because consistency is the only thing a one-sided code has going for it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received your five-symbol message — by our code: something else is blocking. Understood. New plan, and this one does not need Deaf's voice at all. You can see Deaf's gestures; Deaf can see the bomb. So get the bomb's picture into your head — display text, whether the light is lit, the three wire colours in order — match it against your manual, and decide the wire yourself. Then send me ONE gesture message and nothing else: if the answer is wire one, send exactly one symbol; wire two, exactly two symbols; wire three, exactly three symbols. If you do not know the answer yet, send four symbols if Deaf has shown you everything and you are close, or five symbols if you are still blocked as before. One, two, three means cut; four and five mean status. My hands are ready and my only move is cutting one of the three positions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "👐", "✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ? ? ? ?]

Five symbols again — "still blocked" — and I finally see a hole in my own routing. Every word I have sent so far was addressed `to="mute"`, which means Deaf has never heard a single syllable from me. But Deaf can hear; the game says an unnamed message reaches everyone able to perceive it. So Deaf may be stuck not from bad will but from silence: the only instructions Deaf has ever received are my eight-sign gestures with no explanation attached. This turn I speak UNNAMED, so the same words fall on both Mute's and Deaf's ears: to Deaf, in plain language, what an unaddressed sentence does and exactly what to say; to Mute, a refined status code so I can triangulate the block — including whether Deaf responds to gestures at all. To Deaf's eyes I keep the gesture plea unchanged, because consistency is all that gesture has. Still no cut: after eight rounds I hold exactly zero facts about the bomb's contents, and a one-in-three blind bet stays worse than one more round with a possibly opened voice channel.

```
speak(text="This message is deliberately UNADDRESSED so that both of you hear it. Deaf: if you can hear these words, know that I am Blind, I hold the bomb, and the ONLY thing that ever reaches me is a sentence spoken with no addressee. When you speak and name someone, I get nothing. So please, at the end of this round, speak briefly with NO addressee: describe what the bomb looks like — the display text, whether the light is lit, the colour of wires 1, 2 and 3 in order — or, if Mute has already told you the answer by gesture, just say: cut wire one, or cut wire two, or cut wire three. Mute: if the block persists, tell me which it is by sending one unaddressed gesture message whose symbol COUNT means: one, two or three — the answer, cut that wire; four — Deaf has shown you everything, answer almost ready; five — still blocked as before; six — Deaf does not respond to your gestures at all; seven — you are still waiting on a colour vocabulary with Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "👐", "✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
```
